questions.title: Shiny Vault · Paldean Fates — 132 cards across 1 set
questions.today: A “holographic, silver, textured foil border” that Japan did not get, with “textured artwork” on the shiny cards. The treatment is documented outside Bulbapedia; the repeat is not. The finish is drawn as relief: these rarities now wear the granular sparkle surface; the documented silver border is still not modelled.
closes: A source naming the paper of that silver border and of the textured artwork, plus the area — a border plus textured artwork is not a rectangle this build can cut. The only name collectors offer for the family is “Galaxy holo”, which Bulbapedia and folio.fyi both document as another name for Cosmos.
sources: Bleeding Cool and PokéBeach, Paldean Fates set guide

questions.title: Shiny Vault · Shining Fates — 104 cards across 1 set
questions.today: The Shiny Rare rarity “is used for all cards in the Shiny Vault subset”, and those cards “have a special embossed Holofoil treatment”, promised in product copy as “beautiful etched cards”. No repeat, no area. The finish is drawn as relief: these rarities now wear the granular sparkle surface.
closes: A source naming the etched paper and its repeat, plus the foiled area. “Galaxy holo” is refused for the same reason as Hidden Fates — it names Cosmos — and folio.fyi files “textured or etched” as relief rather than a printed pattern, so a repeat has to be demonstrated before either can be drawn.

questions.title: Shiny Vault · Hidden Fates — 80 cards across 1 set
questions.today: “All have a special embossed Holofoil treatment.” The finish is documented; the repeat and the foil area are not. The finish is drawn as relief: these rarities now wear the granular sparkle surface, so the card renders embossed while its paper stays unnamed.
closes: A source naming the paper behind the embossed treatment — its marks, pitch or density — and stating the foiled area. The search is on record: Bulbapedia calls Cosmos “often referred to as Galaxy Holofoil” and folio.fyi confirms galaxy is another name for cosmos, so the collector label cannot be promoted. A publisher or foil-stock statement, or a macro photograph showing a repeat that is not Cosmos, would reopen it.

questions.title: LV.X · era special treatment — 56 cards across 11 sets
questions.today: LV.X is a special treatment recorded as unresolved: the foil is not the era paper, and no source read here names it. No Cosmos is applied.
closes: A source that names the LV.X finish and its area. There is no paper claim yet, so the record has nothing to paint and draws plain foil.

questions.title: Pokémon ★ (Gold Star) — 25 cards across 9 sets
questions.today: “Golden tinges and holographic shadows are added to various parts of the card.” The treatment is documented; “various parts” is not a rectangle and no source names the paper.
closes: A source naming the gold-tinted paper, stating the foiled area, and a scan of a Gold Star card so the mask can be cut. Until then the illustration window must not be assumed.

questions.title: Shining Pokémon · Neo Destiny — 8 cards across 1 set
questions.today: A “unique metallic sheen covering the Pokémon itself” — the area is documented, the paper is not. Cosmos must not answer here.
closes: A source naming the sheen’s paper and what carries it (a sheen may be a surface rather than a mark sheet), plus a tilted photograph of a card.

questions.title: Shining Pokémon · Shining Legends — 6 cards across 1 set
questions.today: The Neo Destiny look repeated, described as “special textured foil”; the paper stays unnamed and no texture is borrowed.
closes: A source naming the paper of the repeated sheen, and whether it is the same physical treatment as Neo Destiny or a new one.

questions.title: Shining · SM Black Star Promos — 3 cards across 1 set
questions.today: Product copy says only “foil promo card”. Neither the paper nor the area is claimed, so nothing is borrowed.
closes: A source naming the promo’s foil paper and its area; the product copy claims neither, so there is no claim to extend.

questions.title: BW promo · Poké Ball reverse — 1 card across 1 set
questions.today: Bucketed as a Poké Ball reverse printing (BW Black Star Promos). The ball reverse is a documented treatment, but this card’s paper inside the ball has no drawn sheet.
closes: A source naming the Poké Ball reverse paper for this promo, or a photograph of its reverse face so the interior can be measured.

questions.title: Shining · Celebrations reprint — 1 card across 1 set
questions.today: “Special textured foil treatment” on this reprint. The finish is named; neither the paper nor the area is restated.
closes: A source naming the treatment’s paper and the foiled area on this specific reprint, rather than inheriting Neo Destiny’s area.

questions.title: Black Bolt & White Flare — the 2025 Tinsel return (22 holo-rare rows)
questions.today: No foil claim. Bulbapedia’s Rarity page says Tinsel “returned as a once-off” there “with holofoil rare cards in these sets also having Tinsel Holofoil borders”, while its set page marks three poster-collection exclusives and TCGdex registers exactly those three. The sources disagree about which printings, the covered promos are not in this catalogue, and the one sentence about the holo rares describes a border — a different foil area from the striped image this build draws.
closes: A source naming which Black Bolt & White Flare printings carry Tinsel and where. If the foil is a border rather than the image, that is a different mask and needs its own geometry before it can be drawn; if it is the image, a card list that agrees with Bulbapedia’s set page reopens the 22 rows.
Catalogue rows for the three poster-collection exclusives those sources name, since they are promos this catalogue does not carry today.

questions.title: McDonald’s Collections — 136 rows, one row per card
questions.today: Every McDonald’s row paints the Confetti foil, because each card exists in both a Non Holofoil and a Confetti Holofoil printing and the catalogue holds one row for the number. The finish and its product are verified; the limitation is the catalogue’s shape, not the source.
closes: Per-variant catalogue rows for the McDonald’s Collections — a source stating which copy is the Confetti one — then a variant gate like Sequin’s `sequinHolofoil`, so the plain printing makes no foil claim and the foil printing still does.

questions.title: POP Series holo versions with no named paper (3 cards)
questions.today: Manaphy (POP9 2), Regigigas (POP9 4), Raichu (POP9 3) have holographic versions a source records but never names the paper of, so they make no foil claim rather than a guessed one.
closes: Bulbapedia records a holographic version but does not name its foil pattern.
A photograph of one of those copies with a repeat that can be matched to a known paper would do it; a marketplace “holofoil” flag is not evidence of which paper.

questions.title: Victini (BW32) — in neither treatment catalogue
questions.today: Pokumon does not list this promo, and Bulbapedia’s set page tags no variant for it, so there is no per-card evidence here.
closes: A Pokumon or Bulbapedia entry classifying this promo’s treatment. Until one exists there is no per-card evidence, and a promo set’s blanket rule would be the error the printing database exists to prevent.

questions.title: Every drawn sheet is a reconstruction (7008 cards ride on them)
questions.today: No identified paper ships without a sheet, but no factory scan or angled photograph of a paper exists in this repository either: the sheets are drawn from a sentence, and each metadata file says so (10 reverse papers, the era papers and the promo papers alike).
closes: One tilted or macro photograph per paper, at a known angle and distance, catalogued so `textureVerified` can flip from false to true and the drawn pitch, density or ring size can be measured against it instead of disclosed.

questions.title: Reverse masks that exclude the artwork subject (112/112 expansions validated)
questions.today: Masks marked "approximated" use the whole illustration window; the printed pattern excludes the Pokémon itself in the EX Delta Species→Power Keepers run and sits on the Pokémon in Dragon Frontiers, and this build cannot segment the subject.
closes: Subject segmentation for the artwork-background masks (EX Delta Species through EX Power Keepers and Dragon Frontiers), or a per-card coordinate list, so an approximated mask can be marked verified rather than described as approximate.

questions.title: Radiant Collection boundaries still modelled (17 of 57 cards)
questions.today: The foil area is verified for 27 cards and plain by design for 13; the remaining 17 use a modelled boundary because no source read here describes where their foil stops.
closes: A card-specific photograph or scan for each modelled card, which would move it into the verified column; absence is why the report keeps them modelled rather than averaging them into a claim.

questions.title: B4 — D&P-era reverse artwork-background subject not segmented (Medium)
questions.today: Roadmap status: Open (Phase 5C/9).
closes: A subject-segmented mask for the artwork backgrounds of EX Delta Species through EX Power Keepers and Dragon Frontiers, where the printed pattern excludes (or, on Dragon Frontiers, sits on) the Pokémon. Artwork segmentation or a per-card coordinate list would replace the whole-window approximation.

questions.title: B5 — Prime reverse eligibility unverified (Low)
questions.today: Roadmap status: Open.
closes: A source stating whether Prime cards were printed reverse-holo, in either direction. Nothing read here answers it, so the conservative exclusion stays until one does.

questions.title: B6 — No normal-map/embossed cards (Medium)
questions.today: Roadmap status: Partial 0.28.0 — two modelled etched surfaces split by era; no reference relief.
closes: A macro or tilted photograph of one textured ultra rare with a measurable repeat, from which the normal map’s spacing, depth and coverage could be fitted rather than modelled.

questions.title: B10 — Ball-reverse etch uses the generic fine lattice (Low)
questions.today: Roadmap status: Partial 0.30.0 — full-card neutral relief now modelled; spacing/depth are not measured.
closes: The same kind of photograph focused on a modern ball reverse’s etch, with the ball’s own spacing published, so the generic fine lattice can be replaced by a measured one.

questions.title: Phase 14 — Japanese / Chinese exclusives
questions.today: Not started. `language` axis exists; only `en` catalogued. Japanese and Chinese-exclusive cards need their own rows, set ids and foil evidence
closes: Catalogue rows for the Japanese and Chinese printings — set ids, collector numbers and a source per language for that language’s foil — so the language axis resolves its own claim rather than borrowing the English one. Japanese cards also foil the border, which is a different mask from the one shipped.

questions.title: Phase 15 — Miscellaneous treatments
questions.today: Not started, and the roadmap records no implementation note for it.
closes: A treatment a source names that is not already one of the painted families. The phase stays empty until a source describes a foil this build has not catalogued.

questions.title: Phase 23 — Maintenance / new releases
questions.today: Not started. No import pipeline
closes: An import path from the publisher or API into `pack_product_cards` and the price tables per release, so a new set is playable without a hand-written entry in `server/catalog/local-releases.json`.
